info.name: web_bff
info.description:
Requests for the Central Dispatch BFF (web_bff). Auth model is bearer pass-through (see docs/adr/0001-bearer-token-passthrough-for-mvp-auth.md): the BFF does not validate the token itself, it forwards whatever Authorization header it receives to CentralDispatch, which is the actual point of validation.

web_bff has no /auth/login route of its own yet (see .scratch/dispatch-detail-proxy/spec.md, Out of Scope), so the "Auth (direct to CentralDispatch)" folder talks to CentralDispatch directly just to obtain a token for testing the BFF's endpoints below it.

Proxies to CentralDispatch's GET /dispatch/{id} (BFF.Presentation/Controllers/DispatchesController.cs). 200 with a DispatchDto body if found, 404 if not, 401 relayed unchanged from CentralDispatch if the bearer token is missing/expired/invalid. See .scratch/dispatch-detail-proxy/spec.md.

item.name: Get dispatch by id - missing token

request.description: Same route with no Authorization header at all. Per the bearer pass-through auth model (ADR-0001), the BFF does not check for a token itself — it forwards the request to CentralDispatch regardless, which rejects it with 401 because its own JWT-bearer auth requires the header. The BFF relays that 401 back unchanged. This asserts CentralDispatch's [Authorize] is still the actual enforcement point, not the BFF.

exec: pm.test("Status is 401 when no bearer token is sent", function () {

request.description: Trips several CreateDispatchRequestValidator rules at once (Price > 0, DropoffDate > PickupDate, 1–12 Vehicles). Demonstrates relay-verbatim on error: the BFF forwards CentralDispatch's ValidationProblemDetails body and 400 status unchanged via DownstreamResponse, instead of reshaping or 500ing.
